arxiv-2101-05584.title: Relativistic effects of rotation in γ \gamma -ray pulsars - Invited Review
arxiv-2101-05584.creator: Osmanov Z.N
arxiv-2101-05584.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Osmanov Z.N. In this paper we consider relativistic effects of rotation in the magnetospheres of γ \gamma -ray pulsars. The paper reviews the progress achieved in this field during the last three decades. For this purpose we examine direct centrifugal acceleration of particles and corresponding limiting factors: constraints due to the curvature radiation and the inverse Compton scattering of electrons against soft photons. Based on the obtained results generation of parametrically excited Langmuir waves and the corresponding Landau-Langmuir-centrifugal drive is studied.

arxiv-2109-01085.title: Cascade R-CNN for MIDOG Challenge
arxiv-2109-01085.creator: Salar Razavi, Fariba Dambandkhameneh, Dimitri Androutsos, Susan Done, April Khademi
arxiv-2109-01085.description: Abstract Mitotic counts are one of the key indicators of breast cancer prognosis. However, accurate mitotic cell counting is still a difficult problem and is labourious. Automated methods have been proposed for this task, but are usually dependent on the training images and show poor performance on unseen domains.

arxiv-2203-12444.title: Volume Approximation of Strongly ℂ {\mathbb{C}} -Convex Domains by Random Polyhedra
arxiv-2203-12444.creator: Siva Athreya, Purvi Gupta, D. Yogeshwaran
arxiv-2203-12444.description: Abstract . Polyhedral-type approximations of convex-like domains in ℂ d {\mathbb{C}}^{d} have been considered recently by the second author. In particular, the decay rate of the error in optimal volume approximation as a function of the number of facets has been obtained.

arxiv-2207-03587.title: Accurate Hellmann–Feynman forces from density functional calculations with augmented Gaussian basis sets
arxiv-2207-03587.creator: Shivesh Pathak, Ignacio Ema López, Alex J. Lee, William P. Bricker, Rafael López Fernández, Susi Lehtola, Joshua A. Rackers
arxiv-2207-03587.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shivesh Pathak, Ignacio Ema López, Alex J. Lee, William P. Bricker, Rafael López Fernández, Susi Lehtola, Joshua A. Rackers. The Hellmann–Feynman (HF) theorem provides a way to compute forces directly from the electron density, enabling efficient force calculations for large systems through machine learning (ML) models for the electron density.

arxiv-2211-10511.title: Knowledge Graph Generation From Text
arxiv-2211-10511.creator: Igor Melnyk, Pierre Dognin, Payel Das
arxiv-2211-10511.description: Abstract In this work we propose a novel end-to-end multi-stage Knowledge Graph (KG) generation system from textual inputs, separating the overall process into two stages. The graph nodes are generated first using pretrained language model, followed by a simple edge construction head, enabling efficient KG extraction from the text.

arxiv-2404-14029.title: Teaching Scrum with a focus on compliance assessment CCS: Software and its engineering Agile software development CCS: Social and professional topics Software engineering education
arxiv-2404-14029.creator: Marco Torchiano, Antonio Vetrò, Riccardo Coppola
arxiv-2404-14029.description: Abstract . The Scrum framework has gained widespread adoption in the industry for its emphasis on collaboration and continuous improvement. However, it has not reached a similar relevance in Software Engineering (SE) curricula. This work reports the experience of five editions of a SE course within an M.Sc. Degree in Computer Engineering.

arxiv-2408-05522.title: Entanglement of Purification as a Measure of Non-Conformality
arxiv-2408-05522.creator: M. Asadi
arxiv-2408-05522.description: Abstract We have studied the entanglement of purification E p E_{p} in a non-conformal holographic model which is a five-dimensional Einstein gravity coupled to a scalar field ϕ \phi with a non-trivial potential V ⁡ ( ϕ ) V(\phi) . The dual 4-dimensional gauge theory is not conformal and exhibits a RG flow between two different fixed points.

arxiv-2505-05276.title: Three-dimensional femtoscopy for proton pairs in heavy-ion collisions
arxiv-2505-05276.creator: Adam Kisiel
arxiv-2505-05276.description: Abstract Femtoscopy, a technique of measuring the size and the dynamics of the system created in heavy-ion collisions is used extensively in experiments at RHIC, LHC, SPS, and the FAIR/GSI. Analysis for pairs of pions is most common, due to their large abundance in the collisions, as well as well-understood theoretical formalism and advanced experimental methodology.

arxiv-2511-07488.title: Quasinormal Mode Spectroscopy via Horizon-Brightened Quantum Optics
arxiv-2511-07488.creator: Ali Övgün
arxiv-2511-07488.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ali Övgün. We develop a quantum optical framework for probing black hole quasinormal modes (QNMs) using two-level atoms in the spirit of the horizon-brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) program. Starting from the QNM contribution to the Wightman function of a scalar field on a static, spherically symmetric black hole background, we derive the response function of a two-level Unruh–DeWitt detector following simple trajectories (static at fixed radius, with comments on radial free fall).

pmc-10618944.creator: Qi Zhang, Jian Li, Lin Shen, Yongsheng Li, Xicheng Wang
pmc-10618944.description: ence of dMMR/MSI-H in patients with CRC has been reported to be 15% (12% with sporadic disease and 3% with Lynch syndrome). The incidence varies by stage, with 20% in stage II, 10%–15% in stage III, and 3%–5% in stage IV2.

pmc-11295528.title: Genomic and induction evidence for bacteriophage contributions to sargassum-bacteria symbioses
pmc-11295528.creator: Alexandra K. Stiffler, Poppy J. Hesketh-Best, Natascha S. Varona, Ashley Zagame, Bailey A. Wallace, Brian E. Lapointe, Cynthia B. Silveira
pmc-11295528.description: BackgroundSymbioses between primary producers and bacteria are crucial for nutrient exchange that fosters host growth and niche adaptation. Yet, how viruses that infect bacteria (phages) influence these bacteria-eukaryote interactions is still largely unknown. Here, we investigate the role of viruses on the genomic diversity and functional adaptations of bacteria associated with pelagic sargassum.

pmc-11345016.title: Carrimycin in a Patient with Acute Myeloid Leukemia Complicated with Life-Threatening Mixed Perianal Infection: A Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-11345016.creator: Xiawan Yang, Yingying Shen, Tonglin Hu, Hangchao Li, Yun Zhang, Yiping Shen, Dijiong Wu
pmc-11345016.description: BackgroundPerianal infection has a high incidence and mortality rate in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Sometimes there is a lack of effective anti-infective treatment regimens.Case PresentationA 58-year-old male diagnosed with AML presented with secondary perianal infection and septic shock upon admission.

pmc-11499812.title: Traditional Chinese Medicine treatment for postoperative axial symptoms of cervical spondylotic myelopathy: a systematic review
pmc-11499812.creator: Xuhao Liu, Xiaolong Yang, Yuanwei Dong, Tiannan Liao, Xin Gou, Jinwen Zou, Liangjuan Ren, Ling Li
pmc-11499812.description: BackgroundAxial symptoms (AS) represent one of the primary complications after cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM) surgery. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), as a complementary and alternative therapy, is widely used in the treatment of postoperative AS in CSM. However, it lacks standardised treatment protocols, uniform therapeutic criteria, assessment methods and a sufficiently in-depth understanding of its mechanisms of action.

pmc-12453181.title: Why does the m6A writer complex require so many proteins?
pmc-12453181.creator: Kiran Pandey, Hui Xian Poh, Samie R. Jaffrey
pmc-12453181.description: The conversion of adenosine to N6-methyladenosine (m6A) is the most common internal modification made to eukaryotic mRNA and is involved in post-transcriptional control of gene expression. When dysregulated, m6A has been linked to a variety of diseases, including cancer. Unlike other RNA methyltransferases, m6A conversion is catalyzed by a multi-protein writer complex with only one catalytic subunit.

pmc-12526982.title: Experimental Evaluation of LoRaWAN Connectivity Reliability in Remote Rural Areas of Mozambique
pmc-12526982.creator: Nelson José Chapungo, Octavian Postolache
pmc-12526982.description: Highlights What are the main findings? LoRaWAN demonstrated high packet delivery reliability (>89%) in a rural Mozambican environment with no electricity or mobile network.Signal strength and quality degraded significantly in lower altitudes, confirming the strong influence of terrain on connectivity. What is the implication of the main finding?

pmc-13274071.title: Compositional design and formulation study of hydroxyapatite–chitosan nanocomposite-modified conventional glass ionomer cement: influence of composition and loading on mechanical, interfacial, and antibacterial properties
pmc-13274071.creator: Neven S Aref, Abeer A El-Fallal, Mohamed A El-Farrash, Fikry M Reicha, Essam E Al-Wakeel
pmc-13274071.description: ObjectivesTo prepare hydroxyapatite/chitosan (HA/CTS) nanocomposites at four weight ratios (85/15, 70/30, 50/50, 30/70) and two concentrations (3 and 5 wt.%), incorporate them into conventional glass ionomer cement (GIC), and evaluate their effect on compressive strength, shear bond strength to dentin, and antibacterial activity.Materials and methodsHA/CTS nanocomposites were synthesized by co-precipitation and characterized by TEM and FTIR.

pmc-13344228.title: AI‐surrogate structure and dose correlation for left anterior descending artery in lung stereotactic body radiotherapy
pmc-13344228.creator: Grace Chang, Quan Chen, Randa Tao, Libing Zhu, Yi Rong, Nathan Y Yu
pmc-13344228.description: BackgroundThe left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery is a critical organ‐at‐risk in thoracic radiotherapy. (a) Definition.— In this section, the term “qualification requirement” means a requirement for testing or other quality assurance demonstration that must be completed by an offeror before award of a contract.
